summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer 12.2 Tutorial - Dragon Dance Production Part Two ## Introduction In this tutorial, we continue to complete the production of the entire Wulong project. After creating the bearded version, we need to create the bearded material. ## Creating Beards I created some beards using XGen in Maya. I will use the top focal angle to render in RNode with a 4K square resolution. ## Preparing UVs in Marvelous Designer Back to Marvelous Designer, in order to make the material easy to use, we need to line up the UV first. We recommend that you line up the UV pieces in Marvelous Designer because 2D panels can also be used to line up the UV. This helps maintain the structure of the face and allows for easy differentiation. For these panels that form the face, I manually place them in a square area. Select the UV panels that have been lined up and place them in the 01 UV panel. Then, select the remaining UV panels in the headboard and use the Auto-Fill UV function to fill them into the UV panel in U1V0. ## Organizing Bearded UV Panels For the bearded version, since I created five types of beards, I will use the length to separate these UV panels and place them according to the same length. Divide these UV panels into five groups. Place the bearded material on the bearded material and set the texture setting to Unified. Then, set the texture angle to 0. Replace the hairline sticker and then adjust the intensity of the hairline sticker. Select multiple UV panels in a whole group, and then shrink them to the size of the bearded sticker. You can observe the texture of the beard in the 3D window to confirm the texture effect. ## Modeling the Dragon’s Head For the dragon's head, I used Maya for modeling and imported it in the OBJ format. Choose Add for the loading type, and choose Add for the object type. Click on the location bar in the upper right corner, paste the dragon's head to the panel, and adjust the rotation position. Repeat this process for the other dragon's head. Select these two dragon's heads, change the color to red, and change the material type to silk. Let's take a look at the effect of pasting the accessories to the material. Open the simulation and drag the nose panel. As the panel is adjusted, the accessories pasted on it will also move along with it, allowing for natural animation during recording. ## Creating Line Effects Next, let's make the line effect. Select the line tool group and open the line window. Use the free line tool to double-click on the straight line on the outline of the film, and add a line to the outline of the eyebrow film. Marvelous Designer has six different line types. I will choose the Overlock preset, increase the strength in the information, and modify the width, length, and thickness of the line, as well as the color. You can go to the Connect store to download more line types or define your own OBJ file as a line type. For the line in the eye area, I will use the Diamond Satin style downloaded from Connect and then modify the corresponding properties. Change the color to gold and the material type to silk. The nose part will use the same line as the eyebrow version. Next, apply the Rise line downloaded from the Connect store to the inner line on the lip version, and modify the corresponding properties as needed. Select the side eyebrow version and create an inner line using the Inner Line tool. Remember to select the Extend inner line option. You can choose the color as you like and add the background color at the top of the inner line. ## Finalizing Eyebrow Shape Now create an Overlock bridge, adding the outline of the eyebrow film and inner line at the same time. Adjust various properties and color to present the overall shape of the eyebrow. I will draw the shape of the eyebrow using the outline as a guide. ## Applying Fabric to the Face For the skin of the face, I will use Substance's Flecked Tartan fabric. You can find it in the Substance folder in the Library window. Drag it to the fabric type of the face panel to replace the original fabric texture. After selecting this fabric type, you can modify some of the properties of Substance in the property editor. ## Creating the Dragon's Body I made the bones of the body in Maya, tied the bones, and created the animation. To be closer to the structure of the dragon in the real world, I used round pieces as the bones. The body structure of the dragon has a similar support structure with a stick at the bottom that the performer will use to perform the dragon's dance. The animation will be exported in the Alembic cache format and used in Marvelous Designer. Enter the Alembic file, and we can see the animation in the animation editor at the bottom. ## Setting Up the Round Sheets Create a round sheet according to the size made in Maya. Stick each round sheet on the round sheet and repeat the steps. All round sheets are placed in the 3D window, and then switch to the Stabilizer tool. Add a Stabilizer to the top of the grid on the double sheet outline. Right-click on any Stabilizer and select Stabilize all Stabilizers on the virtual model. This way, the sheet will move along with the round sheet. Then, create a rectangular sheet with the round sheet as the width value. Set the height to 1000 mm, as the diameter between each round sheet was set in Maya. For arranging these sheets, we will create an arrangement point and arrangement board for convenience. ## Creating Arrangement Points Go to the main menu, navigate to Virtual Model, and open the Virtual Model Editor. Add an arrangement board under the arrangement label bar. Place it between the two round sheets and rotate it. Increase the height of X and Y. Then, add an arrangement point and set it to the arrangement board just created. Open the display arrangement point, select the rectangular sheet, and click on the arrangement point to arrange the sheet. Created the marking line between the wheel plates and the sewing line between the panels. ## Examining the Material Examine the material by changing it to Nylon Canvas and opening the simulation. Copy and paste the body version to repeat the previous operation. After the model is finished, I will use the animation editor to record the transformation process of the five dragons. ## Preparing for Animation Recording Before recording, ensure that all the fixed needles are secured to the virtual model. Change the simulation attribute to animation, then go to the attribute editor, turn off the conflict on the ground, and set the gravity to 0. Set the air resistance to 3 and the scene time change to 2 for a more stable simulation effect. After these adjustments, click the record button to begin. Marvelous Designer will record the animation for you. ## Conclusion Now, please check the final effect. After the action is modified, you can export the file for subsequent adjustment and rendering. If you found this tutorial helpful, please like and subscribe to our channel. Thank you for watching, and take care of yourselves! Goodbye, everyone! ```
